_comment: JAZZ comping patterns (voicing space), Phase ML.4. Encoded from the comping grids in docs/idiom-research/genre-jazz-blues-classical.md section 3 -- rhythm archetypes and voicing techniques (shells, rootless 3-5-7-9, drop-2) are freely copyable; these realizations are original and no player's chorus is transcribed. Density stays at or under 2.5 hits per bar outside the four-to-the-bar pattern (section 3 rule) and root-position blocks on every downbeat are avoided (section 8 trap 2).

provenance.inspiration: style of swing-era rhythm guitar: four short three-note shells per bar, quarters never swung, beats two and four a touch stronger (original realization)
the Charleston rhythm comping grid (section 3) -- downbeat plus the and-of-two, shell into a rootless answer (rhythm archetype, original voicing plan)
style of small-group piano comping: rootless four-note voicings on the and-of-two and beat three, the second bar pushing the next chord on the and-of-four (original realization)
style of angular one-stab-per-bar piano punctuation: the stab moves to a different beat each bar and the rest of the bar is silence (original realization)
style of ballad piano comping under 90 BPM: two legato rootless voicings a half-bar apart, A-form answered by B-form (original realization)
